     1→import type { GLOBAL_OBJ } from '@sentry/core';
     2→import type { SentryWebpackPluginOptions } from '@sentry/webpack-plugin';
     3→export type ExportedNextConfig = NextConfigObject | NextConfigFunction;
     4→type NextRewrite = {
     5→    source: string;
     6→    destination: string;
     7→};
     8→export interface WebpackPluginInstance {
     9→    [index: string]: unknown;
    10→    apply: (compiler: unknown) => void;
    11→}
    12→export type NextConfigObject = {
    13→    webpack?: WebpackConfigFunction | null;
    14→    target?: 'server' | 'experimental-serverless-trace';
    15→    distDir?: string;
    16→    assetPrefix?: string;
    17→    basePath?: string;
    18→    publicRuntimeConfig?: {
    19→        [key: string]: unknown;
    20→    };
    21→    pageExtensions?: string[];
    22→    output?: string;
    23→    rewrites?: () => Promise<NextRewrite[] | {
    24→        beforeFiles?: NextRewrite[];
    25→        afterFiles?: NextRewrite[];
    26→        fallback?: NextRewrite[];
    27→    }>;
    28→    cacheComponents?: boolean;
    29→    experimental?: {
    30→        instrumentationHook?: boolean;
    31→        clientTraceMetadata?: string[];
    32→        serverComponentsExternalPackages?: string[];
    33→        outputFileTracingIncludes?: Record<string, string[]>;
    34→        sri?: {
    35→            algorithm?: string;
    36→        };
    37→    };
    38→    productionBrowserSourceMaps?: boolean;
    39→    env?: Record<string, string>;
    40→    serverExternalPackages?: string[];
    41→    outputFileTracingIncludes?: Record<string, string[]>;
    42→    turbopack?: TurbopackOptions;
    43→    compiler?: {
    44→        runAfterProductionCompile?: (context: {
    45→            distDir: string;
    46→            projectDir: string;
    47→        }) => Promise<void> | void;
    48→    };
    49→};
    50→export type SentryBuildWebpackOptions = {
    51→    /**
    52→     * Automatically instrument Next.js data fetching methods and Next.js API routes with error and performance monitoring.
    53→     * Defaults to `true`.
    54→     */
    55→    autoInstrumentServerFunctions?: boolean;
    56→    /**
    57→     * Automatically instrument Next.js middleware with error and performance monitoring. Defaults to `true`.
    58→     */
    59→    autoInstrumentMiddleware?: boolean;
    60→    /**
    61→     * Automatically instrument components in the `app` directory with error monitoring. Defaults to `true`.
    62→     */
    63→    autoInstrumentAppDirectory?: boolean;
    64→    /**
    65→     * Automatically create cron monitors in Sentry for your Vercel Cron Jobs if configured via `vercel.json`.
    66→     *
    67→     * Defaults to `false`.
    68→     */
    69→    automaticVercelMonitors?: boolean;
    70→    /**
    71→     * Exclude certain serverside API routes or pages from being instrumented with Sentry during build-time. This option
    72→     * takes an array of strings or regular expressions. This options also affects pages in the `app` directory.
    73→     *
    74→     * NOTE: Pages should be specified as routes (`/animals` or `/api/animals/[animalType]/habitat`), not filepaths
    75→     * (`pages/animals/index.js` or `.\src\pages\api\animals\[animalType]\habitat.tsx`), and strings must be be a full,
    76→     * exact match.
    77→     *
    78→     * Notice: If you build Next.js with turbopack, the Sentry SDK will no longer apply build-time instrumentation and
    79→     * purely rely on Next.js telemetry features, meaning that this option will effectively no-op.
    80→     */
    81→    excludeServerRoutes?: Array<RegExp | string>;
    82→    /**
    83→     * Disables automatic injection of Sentry's Webpack configuration.
    84→     *
    85→     * By default, the Sentry Next.js SDK injects its own Webpack configuration to enable features such as
    86→     * source map upload and automatic instrumentation. Set this option to `true` if you want to prevent
    87→     * the SDK from modifying your Webpack config (for example, if you want to handle Sentry integration manually
    88→     * or if you are on an older version of Next.js while using Turbopack).
    89→     */
    90→    disableSentryConfig?: boolean;
    91→    /**
    92→     * Tree-shaking options to help reduce the size of the Sentry SDK bundle.
    93→     */
    94→    treeshake?: {
    95→        /**
    96→         * Removes Sentry SDK logger statements from the bundle. Note that this doesn't affect Sentry Logs.
    97→         */
    98→        removeDebugLogging?: boolean;
    99→        /**
   100→         * Setting this to true will treeshake any SDK code that is related to tracing and performance monitoring.
   101→         */
   102→        removeTracing?: boolean;
   103→        /**
   104→         * Setting this flag to `true` will tree shake any SDK code related to capturing iframe content with Session Replay.
   105→         * It's only relevant when using Session Replay. Enable this flag if you don't want to record any iframes.
   106→         * This has no effect if you did not add `replayIntegration`.
   107→         */
   108→        excludeReplayIframe?: boolean;
   109→        /**
   110→         * Setting this flag to `true` will tree shake any SDK code related to capturing shadow dom elements with Session Replay.
   111→         * It's only relevant when using Session Replay.
   112→         * Enable this flag if you don't want to record any shadow DOM elements.
   113→         * This has no effect if you did not add `replayIntegration`.
   114→         */
   115→        excludeReplayShadowDOM?: boolean;
   116→        /**
   117→         * Setting this flag to `true` will tree shake any SDK code that is related to the included compression web worker for Session Replay.
   118→         * It's only relevant when using Session Replay.
   119→         * Enable this flag if you want to host a compression worker yourself.
   120→         * See Using a Custom Compression Worker for details.
   121→         * We don't recommend enabling this flag unless you provide a custom worker URL.
   122→         * This has no effect if you did not add `replayIntegration`.
   123→         */
   124→        excludeReplayCompressionWorker?: boolean;
   125→    };
   126→    /**
   127→     * Options to be passed directly to the Sentry Webpack Plugin (`@sentry/webpack-plugin`) that ships with the Sentry SDK.
   128→     * You can use this option to override any options the SDK passes to the Webpack plugin.
   129→     *
   130→     * Please note that this option is unstable and may change in a breaking way in any release.
   131→     */
   132→    unstable_sentryWebpackPluginOptions?: SentryWebpackPluginOptions;
   133→    /**
   134→     * Options related to react component name annotations.
   135→     * Disabled by default, unless a value is set for this option.
   136→     * When enabled, your app's DOM will automatically be annotated during build-time with their respective component names.
   137→     * This will unlock the capability to search for Replays in Sentry by component name, as well as see component names in breadcrumbs and performance monitoring.
   138→     * Please note that this feature is not currently supported by the esbuild bundler plugins, and will only annotate React components
   139→     */
   140→    reactComponentAnnotation?: {
   141→        /**
   142→         * Whether the component name annotate plugin should be enabled or not.
   143→         */
   144→        enabled?: boolean;
   145→        /**
   146→         * A list of strings representing the names of components to ignore. The plugin will not apply `data-sentry` annotations on the DOM element for these components.
   147→         */
   148→        ignoredComponents?: string[];
   149→    };
   150→};
   151→export type SentryBuildOptions = {
   152→    /**
   153→     * The slug of the Sentry organization associated with the app.
   154→     *
   155→     * This value can also be specified via the `SENTRY_ORG` environment variable.
   156→     */
   157→    org?: string;
   158→    /**
   159→     * The slug of the Sentry project associated with the app.
   160→     *
   161→     * This value can also be specified via the `SENTRY_PROJECT` environment variable.
   162→     */
   163→    project?: string | string[];
   164→    /**
   165→     * The authentication token to use for all communication with Sentry.
   166→     * Can be obtained from https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/settings/auth-tokens/.
   167→     *
   168→     * This value can also be specified via the `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable.
   169→     */
   170→    authToken?: string;
   171→    /**
   172→     * The base URL of your Sentry instance. Use this if you are using a self-hosted
   173→     * or Sentry instance other than sentry.io.
   174→     *
   175→     * This value can also be set via the `SENTRY_URL` environment variable.
   176→     *
   177→     * Defaults to https://sentry.io/, which is the correct value for SaaS customers.
   178→     */
   179→    sentryUrl?: string;
   180→    /**
   181→     * Headers added to every outgoing network request.
   182→     */
   183→    headers?: Record<string, string>;
   184→    /**
   185→     * If set to true, internal plugin errors and performance data will be sent to Sentry.
   186→     *
   187→     * At Sentry we like to use Sentry ourselves to deliver faster and more stable products.
   188→     * We're very careful of what we're sending. We won't collect anything other than error
   189→     * and high-level performance data. We will never collect your code or any details of the
   190→     * projects in which you're using this plugin.
   191→     *
   192→     * Defaults to `true`.
   193→     */
   194→    telemetry?: boolean;
   195→    /**
   196→     * Suppresses all Sentry SDK build logs.
   197→     *
   198→     * Defaults to `false`.
   199→     */
   200→    silent?: boolean;
   201→    /**
   202→     * Prints additional debug information about the SDK and uploading source maps when building the application.
   203→     *
   204→     * Defaults to `false`.
   205→     */
   206→    debug?: boolean;
   207→    /**
   208→     * Options for source maps uploading.
   209→     */
   210→    sourcemaps?: {
   211→        /**
   212→         * Disable any functionality related to source maps.
   213→         */
   214→        disable?: boolean;
   215→        /**
   216→         * A glob or an array of globs that specifies the build artifacts that should be uploaded to Sentry.
   217→         *
   218→         * If this option is not specified, the plugin will try to upload all JavaScript files and source map files that are created during build.
   219→         *
   220→         * The globbing patterns follow the implementation of the `glob` package. (https://www.npmjs.com/package/glob)
   221→         *
   222→         * Use the `debug` option to print information about which files end up being uploaded.
   223→         */
   224→        assets?: string | string[];
   225→        /**
   226→         * A glob or an array of globs that specifies which build artifacts should not be uploaded to Sentry.
   227→         *
   228→         * The SDK automatically ignores Next.js internal files that don't have source maps (such as manifest files)
   229→         * to prevent "Could not determine source map" warnings. Your custom patterns are merged with these defaults.
   230→         *
   231→         * The globbing patterns follow the implementation of the `glob` package. (https://www.npmjs.com/package/glob)
   232→         *
   233→         * Use the `debug` option to print information about which files end up being uploaded.
   234→         */
   235→        ignore?: string | string[];
   236→        /**
   237→         * Toggle whether generated source maps within your Next.js build folder should be automatically deleted after being uploaded to Sentry.
   238→         *
   239→         * Defaults to `true`.
   240→         */
   241→        deleteSourcemapsAfterUpload?: boolean;
   242→        /**
   243→         * A glob or an array of globs that specifies which source map files should be deleted after being uploaded to Sentry.
   244→         *
   245→         * When set, this overrides the default deletion behavior of `deleteSourcemapsAfterUpload`.
   246→         *
   247→         * Use this option when you need fine-grained control over which source maps are deleted.
   248→         *
   249→         * @example
   250→         * ```javascript
   251→         * withSentryConfig(nextConfig, {
   252→         *   sourcemaps: {
   253→         *     filesToDeleteAfterUpload: ['.next/static/**\/*.map'],
   254→         *   },
   255→         * });
   256→         * ```
   257→         */
   258→        filesToDeleteAfterUpload?: string | string[];
   259→        /**
   260→         * Hook to rewrite the `sources` field inside the source map before being uploaded to Sentry. Does not modify the actual source map.
   261→         *
   262→         * The hook receives the following arguments:
   263→         * - `source` - the source file path from the source map's `sources` field
   264→         * - `map` - the source map object
   265→         * - `context` - an optional object containing `mapDir`, the absolute path to the directory of the source map file
   266→         *
   267→         * If not provided, the SDK defaults to stripping webpack-specific prefixes (`webpack://_N_E/`).
   268→         *
   269→         * Defaults to making all sources relative to `process.cwd()` while building.
   270→         */
   271→        rewriteSources?: (source: string, map: any, context?: {
   272→            mapDir: string;
   273→        }) => string;
   274→    };
   275→    /**
   276→     * Options related to managing the Sentry releases for a build.
   277→     *
   278→     * More info: https://docs.sentry.io/product/releases/
   279→     */
   280→    release?: {
   281→        /**
   282→         * Unique identifier for the release you want to create.
   283→         *
   284→         * This value can also be specified via the `SENTRY_RELEASE` environment variable.
   285→         *
   286→         * Defaults to automatically detecting a value for your environment.
   287→         * This includes values for Cordova, Heroku, AWS CodeBuild, CircleCI, Xcode, and Gradle, and otherwise uses the git `HEAD`'s commit SHA.
   288→         * (the latter requires access to git CLI and for the root directory to be a valid repository)
   289→         *
   290→         * If you didn't provide a value and the plugin can't automatically detect one, no release will be created.
   291→         */
   292→        name?: string;
   293→        /**
   294→         * Whether the plugin should create a release on Sentry during the build.
   295→         * Note that a release may still appear in Sentry even if this is value is `false` because any Sentry event that has a release value attached will automatically create a release.
   296→         * (for example via the `inject` option)
   297→         *
   298→         * Defaults to `true`.
   299→         */
   300→        create?: boolean;
   301→        /**
   302→         * Whether the Sentry release should be automatically finalized (meaning an end timestamp is added) after the build ends.
   303→         *
   304→         * Defaults to `true`.
   305→         */
   306→        finalize?: boolean;
   307→        /**
   308→         * Unique identifier for the distribution, used to further segment your release.
   309→         * Usually your build number.
   310→         */
   311→        dist?: string;
   312→        /**
   313→         * Version control system remote name.
   314→         *
   315→         * This value can also be specified via the `SENTRY_VSC_REMOTE` environment variable.
   316→         *
   317→         * Defaults to 'origin'.
   318→         */
   319→        vcsRemote?: string;
   320→        /**
   321→         * Associates the release with its commits in Sentry.
   322→         */
   323→        setCommits?: ({
   324→            /**
   325→             * Automatically sets `commit` and `previousCommit`. Sets `commit` to `HEAD`
   326→             * and `previousCommit` as described in the option's documentation.
   327→             *
   328→             * If you set this to `true`, manually specified `commit` and `previousCommit`
   329→             * options will be overridden. It is best to not specify them at all if you
   330→             * set this option to `true`.
   331→             */
   332→            auto: true;
   333→            repo?: undefined;
   334→            commit?: undefined;
   335→        } | {
   336→            auto?: false | undefined;
   337→            /**
   338→             * The full repo name as defined in Sentry.
   339→             *
   340→             * Required if the `auto` option is not set to `true`.
   341→             */
   342→            repo: string;
   343→            /**
   344→             * The current (last) commit in the release.
   345→             *
   346→             * Required if the `auto` option is not set to `true`.
   347→             */
   348→            commit: string;
   349→        }) & {
   350→            /**
   351→             * The commit before the beginning of this release (in other words,
   352→             * the last commit of the previous release).
   353→             *
   354→             * Defaults to the last commit of the previous release in Sentry.
   355→             *
   356→             * If there was no previous release, the last 10 commits will be used.
   357→             */
   358→            previousCommit?: string;
   359→            /**
   360→             * If the flag is to `true` and the previous release commit was not found
   361→             * in the repository, the plugin creates a release with the default commits
   362→             * count instead of failing the command.
   363→             *
   364→             * Defaults to `false`.
   365→             */
   366→            ignoreMissing?: boolean;
   367→            /**
   368→             * If this flag is set, the setCommits step will not fail and just exit
   369→             * silently if no new commits for a given release have been found.
   370→             *
   371→             * Defaults to `false`.
   372→             */
   373→            ignoreEmpty?: boolean;
   374→        };
   375→        /**
   376→         * Adds deployment information to the release in Sentry.
   377→         */
   378→        deploy?: {
   379→            /**
   380→             * Environment for this release. Values that make sense here would
   381→             * be `production` or `staging`.
   382→             */
   383→            env: string;
   384→            /**
   385→             * Deployment start time in Unix timestamp (in seconds) or ISO 8601 format.
   386→             */
   387→            started?: number | string;
   388→            /**
   389→             * Deployment finish time in Unix timestamp (in seconds) or ISO 8601 format.
   390→             */
   391→            finished?: number | string;
   392→            /**
   393→             * Deployment duration (in seconds). Can be used instead of started and finished.
   394→             */
   395→            time?: number;
   396→            /**
   397→             * Human readable name for the deployment.
   398→             */
   399→            name?: string;
   400→            /**
   401→             * URL that points to the deployment.
   402→             */
   403→            url?: string;
   404→        };
   405→    };
   406→    /**
   407→     * A key that is used to identify the application in the Sentry bundler plugins.
   408→     * This key is used by the `thirdPartyErrorFilterIntegration` to filter out errors
   409→     * originating from third-party scripts.
   410→     *
   411→     * For webpack builds, this is forwarded to the `@sentry/webpack-plugin`.
   412→     * For Turbopack builds, this injects module metadata via a custom loader.
   413→     *
   414→     * @see https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/configuration/filtering/#using-thirdpartyerrorfilterintegration
   415→     */
   416→    applicationKey?: string;
   417→    /**
   418→     * Options to configure various bundle size optimizations related to the Sentry SDK.
   419→     */
   420→    bundleSizeOptimizations?: {
   421→        /**
   422→         * If set to `true`, the Sentry SDK will attempt to treeshake (remove) any debugging code within itself during the build.
   423→         * Note that the success of this depends on tree shaking being enabled in your build tooling.
   424→         *
   425→         * Setting this option to `true` will disable features like the SDK's `debug` option.
   426→         */
   427→        excludeDebugStatements?: boolean;
   428→        /**
   429→         * If set to `true`, the Sentry SDK will attempt to treeshake (remove) code within itself that is related to tracing and performance monitoring.
   430→         * Note that the success of this depends on tree shaking being enabled in your build tooling.
   431→         * **Notice:** Do not enable this when you're using any performance monitoring-related SDK features (e.g. `Sentry.startTransaction()`).
   432→         */
   433→        excludeTracing?: boolean;
   434→        /**
   435→         * If set to `true`, the Sentry SDK will attempt to treeshake (remove) code related to the SDK's Session Replay Shadow DOM recording functionality.
   436→         * Note that the success of this depends on tree shaking being enabled in your build tooling.
   437→         *
   438→         * This option is safe to be used when you do not want to capture any Shadow DOM activity via Sentry Session Replay.
   439→         */
   440→        excludeReplayShadowDom?: boolean;
   441→        /**
   442→         * If set to `true`, the Sentry SDK will attempt to treeshake (remove) code related to the SDK's Session Replay `iframe` recording functionality.
   443→         * Note that the success of this depends on tree shaking being enabled in your build tooling.
   444→         *
   445→         * You can safely do this when you do not want to capture any `iframe` activity via Sentry Session Replay.
   446→         */
   447→        excludeReplayIframe?: boolean;
   448→        /**
   449→         * If set to `true`, the Sentry SDK will attempt to treeshake (remove) code related to the SDK's Session Replay's Compression Web Worker.
   450→         * Note that the success of this depends on tree shaking being enabled in your build tooling.
   451→         *
   452→         * **Notice:** You should only use this option if you manually host a compression worker and configure it in your Sentry Session Replay integration config via the `workerUrl` option.
   453→         */
   454→        excludeReplayWorker?: boolean;
   455→    };
   456→    /**
   457→     * Options related to react component name annotations.
   458→     * Disabled by default, unless a value is set for this option.
   459→     * When enabled, your app's DOM will automatically be annotated during build-time with their respective component names.
   460→     * This will unlock the capability to search for Replays in Sentry by component name, as well as see component names in breadcrumbs and performance monitoring.
   461→     * Please note that this feature is not currently supported by the esbuild bundler plugins, and will only annotate React components
   462→     *
   463→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.reactComponentAnnotation` instead.
   464→     */
   465→    reactComponentAnnotation?: {
   466→        /**
   467→         * Whether the component name annotate plugin should be enabled or not.
   468→         */
   469→        enabled?: boolean;
   470→        /**
   471→         * A list of strings representing the names of components to ignore. The plugin will not apply `data-sentry` annotations on the DOM element for these components.
   472→         */
   473→        ignoredComponents?: string[];
   474→    };
   475→    /**
   476→     * Options to be passed directly to the Sentry Webpack Plugin (`@sentry/webpack-plugin`) that ships with the Sentry Next.js SDK.
   477→     * You can use this option to override any options the SDK passes to the webpack plugin.
   478→     *
   479→     * Please note that this option is unstable and may change in a breaking way in any release.
   480→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.unstable_sentryWebpackPluginOptions` instead.
   481→     */
   482→    unstable_sentryWebpackPluginOptions?: SentryWebpackPluginOptions;
   483→    /**
   484→     * Include Next.js-internal code and code from dependencies when uploading source maps.
   485→     *
   486→     * Note: Enabling this option can lead to longer build times.
   487→     * Disabling this option will leave you without readable stacktraces for dependencies and Next.js-internal code.
   488→     *
   489→     * Defaults to `false`.
   490→     *
   491→     * This option applies to both webpack and turbopack builds.
   492→     */
   493→    widenClientFileUpload?: boolean;
   494→    /**
   495→     * Automatically instrument Next.js data fetching methods and Next.js API routes with error and performance monitoring.
   496→     * Defaults to `true`.
   497→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.autoInstrumentServerFunctions` instead.
   498→     */
   499→    autoInstrumentServerFunctions?: boolean;
   500→    /**
   501→     * Automatically instrument Next.js middleware with error and performance monitoring. Defaults to `true`.
   502→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.autoInstrumentMiddleware` instead.
   503→     */
   504→    autoInstrumentMiddleware?: boolean;
   505→    /**
   506→     * Automatically instrument components in the `app` directory with error monitoring. Defaults to `true`.
   507→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.autoInstrumentAppDirectory` instead.
   508→     */
   509→    autoInstrumentAppDirectory?: boolean;
   510→    /**
   511→     * Exclude certain serverside API routes or pages from being instrumented with Sentry during build-time. This option
   512→     * takes an array of strings or regular expressions. This options also affects pages in the `app` directory.
   513→     *
   514→     * NOTE: Pages should be specified as routes (`/animals` or `/api/animals/[animalType]/habitat`), not filepaths
   515→     * (`pages/animals/index.js` or `.\src\pages\api\animals\[animalType]\habitat.tsx`), and strings must be be a full,
   516→     * exact match.
   517→     *
   518→     * Notice: If you build Next.js with turbopack, the Sentry SDK will no longer apply build-time instrumentation and
   519→     * purely rely on Next.js telemetry features, meaning that this option will effectively no-op.
   520→     *
   521→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.excludeServerRoutes` instead.
   522→     */
   523→    excludeServerRoutes?: Array<RegExp | string>;
   524→    /**
   525→     * Tunnel Sentry requests through this route on the Next.js server, to circumvent ad-blockers blocking Sentry events
   526→     * from being sent. This option should be a path (for example: '/error-monitoring').
   527→     *
   528→     * - Pass `true` to auto-generate a random, ad-blocker-resistant route for each build
   529→     * - Pass a string path (e.g., '/monitoring') to use a custom route
   530→     *
   531→     * NOTE: This feature only works with Next.js 11+
   532→     */
   533→    tunnelRoute?: string | boolean;
   534→    /**
   535→     * Tree shakes Sentry SDK logger statements from the bundle.
   536→     *
   537→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.treeshake.removeDebugLogging` instead.
   538→     */
   539→    disableLogger?: boolean;
   540→    /**
   541→     * Automatically create cron monitors in Sentry for your Vercel Cron Jobs if configured via `vercel.json`.
   542→     *
   543→     * Defaults to `false`.
   544→     *
   545→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.automaticVercelMonitors` instead.
   546→     */
   547→    automaticVercelMonitors?: boolean;
   548→    /**
   549→     * When an error occurs during release creation or sourcemaps upload, the plugin will call this function.
   550→     *
   551→     * By default, the plugin will simply throw an error, thereby stopping the bundling process.
   552→     * If an `errorHandler` callback is provided, compilation will continue, unless an error is
   553→     * thrown in the provided callback.
   554→     *
   555→     * To allow compilation to continue but still emit a warning, set this option to the following:
   556→     *
   557→     * ```js
   558→     * (err) => {
   559→     *   console.warn(err);
   560→     * }
   561→     * ```
   562→     */
   563→    errorHandler?: (err: Error) => void;
   564→    /**
   565→     * Suppress the warning about the `onRouterTransitionStart` hook.
   566→     */
   567→    suppressOnRouterTransitionStartWarning?: boolean;
   568→    /**
   569→     * Disables automatic injection of the route manifest into the client bundle.
   570→     *
   571→     * @deprecated Use `routeManifestInjection: false` instead.
   572→     *
   573→     * @default false
   574→     */
   575→    disableManifestInjection?: boolean;
   576→    /**
   577→     * Options for the route manifest injection feature.
   578→     *
   579→     * The route manifest is a build-time generated mapping of your Next.js App Router
   580→     * routes that enables Sentry to group transactions by parameterized route names
   581→     * (e.g., `/users/:id` instead of `/users/123`, `/users/456`, etc.).
   582→     *
   583→     * Set to `false` to disable route manifest injection entirely.
   584→     *
   585→     * @example
   586→     * ```js
   587→     * // Disable route manifest injection
   588→     * routeManifestInjection: false
   589→     *
   590→     * // Exclude specific routes
   591→     * routeManifestInjection: {
   592→     *   exclude: [
   593→     *     '/admin',           // Exact match
   594→     *     /^\/internal\//,    // Regex: all routes starting with /internal/
   595→     *     /\/secret-/,        // Regex: any route containing /secret-
   596→     *   ]
   597→     * }
   598→     *
   599→     * // Exclude using a function
   600→     * routeManifestInjection: {
   601→     *   exclude: (route) => route.includes('hidden')
   602→     * }
   603→     * ```
   604→     */
   605→    routeManifestInjection?: false | {
   606→        /**
   607→         * Exclude specific routes from the route manifest.
   608→         *
   609→         * Use this option to prevent certain routes from being included in the client bundle's
   610→         * route manifest. This is useful for:
   611→         * - Hiding confidential or unreleased feature routes
   612→         * - Excluding internal/admin routes you don't want exposed
   613→         * - Reducing bundle size by omitting rarely-used routes
   614→         *
   615→         * Can be specified as:
   616→         * - An array of strings (exact match) or RegExp patterns
   617→         * - A function that receives a route path and returns `true` to exclude it
   618→         */
   619→        exclude?: Array<string | RegExp> | ((route: string) => boolean);
   620→    };
   621→    /**
   622→     * Disables automatic injection of Sentry's Webpack configuration.
   623→     *
   624→     * By default, the Sentry Next.js SDK injects its own Webpack configuration to enable features such as
   625→     * source map upload and automatic instrumentation. Set this option to `true` if you want to prevent
   626→     * the SDK from modifying your Webpack config (for example, if you want to handle Sentry integration manually
   627→     * or if you are on an older version of Next.js while using Turbopack).
   628→     *
   629→     * @deprecated Use `webpack.disableSentryConfig` instead.
   630→     *
   631→     * @default false
   632→     */
   633→    disableSentryWebpackConfig?: boolean;
   634→    /**
   635→     * When true (and Next.js >= 15), use the runAfterProductionCompile hook to consolidate sourcemap uploads
   636→     * into a single operation after builds complete, reducing build time.
   637→     *
   638→     * When false, use the traditional approach of uploading sourcemaps during each webpack build. For Turbopack no sourcemaps will be uploaded.
   639→     *
   640→     * @default true for Turbopack, false for Webpack
   641→     */
   642→    useRunAfterProductionCompileHook?: boolean;
   643→    /**
   644→     * Contains a set of experimental flags that might change in future releases. These flags enable
   645→     * features that are still in development and may be modified, renamed, or removed without notice.
   646→     * Use with caution in production environments.
   647→     */
   648→    _experimental?: Partial<{
   649→        thirdPartyOriginStackFrames?: boolean;
   650→        /**
   651→         * Automatically instrument Vercel Cron Jobs in the App Router with Sentry Cron Monitors.
   652→         * When enabled, the SDK will detect Vercel cron requests and create check-ins in Sentry.
   653→         * Requires cron jobs to be configured in `vercel.json`.
   654→         */
   655→        vercelCronsMonitoring?: boolean;
   656→        /**
   657→         * Application key used by `thirdPartyErrorFilterIntegration` to distinguish
   658→         * first-party code from third-party code in Turbopack builds.
   659→         *
   660→         * When set, a Turbopack loader injects `_sentryModuleMetadata` into every
   661→         * first-party module, mirroring what `@sentry/webpack-plugin` does for
   662→         * webpack builds via its `moduleMetadata` / `applicationKey` option.
   663→         *
   664→         * Requires Next.js 16+
   665→         *
   666→         * @deprecated Use the top-level `applicationKey` option instead, which works for both webpack and Turbopack builds.
   667→         */
   668→        turbopackApplicationKey?: string;
   669→        /**
   670→         * Options for React component name annotation in Turbopack builds.
   671→         * When enabled, JSX elements are annotated with `data-sentry-component`,
   672→         * `data-sentry-element`, and `data-sentry-source-file` attributes.
   673→         * Requires Next.js 16+.
   674→         */
   675→        turbopackReactComponentAnnotation?: {
   676→            enabled?: boolean;
   677→            ignoredComponents?: string[];
   678→        };
   679→        /**
   680→         * EXPERIMENTAL: Wire up orchestrion diagnostics-channel instrumentation at build time.
   681→         *
   682→         * When enabled, `withSentryConfig` injects the orchestrion code-transform loader for bundled
   683→         * server packages and keeps the remaining instrumented packages external so the runtime module
   684→         * hook picks them up. You must still call `Sentry.experimentalUseDiagnosticsChannelInjection()`
   685→         * in your server config to record spans.
   686→         *
   687→         * Turbopack support requires Next.js 16+; the webpack path works on earlier versions.
   688→         *
   689→         * @experimental May change or be removed in any release.
   690→         */
   691→        useDiagnosticsChannelInjection?: boolean;
   692→    }>;
   693→    /**
   694→     * Options related to webpack builds, has no effect if you are using Turbopack.
   695→     */
   696→    webpack?: SentryBuildWebpackOptions;
   697→};
   698→export type NextConfigFunction = (phase: string, defaults: {
   699→    defaultConfig: NextConfigObject;
   700→}) => NextConfigObject | PromiseLike<NextConfigObject>;
   701→/**
   702→ * Webpack config
   703→ */
   704→export type IgnoreWarningsOption = ({
   705→    module?: RegExp;
   706→    message?: RegExp;
   707→} | ((webpackError: {
   708→    module?: {
   709→        readableIdentifier: (requestShortener: unknown) => string;
   710→    };
   711→    message: string;
   712→}, compilation: {
   713→    requestShortener: unknown;
   714→}) => boolean))[];
   715→export type WebpackConfigFunction = (config: WebpackConfigObject, options: BuildContext) => WebpackConfigObject;
   716→export type WebpackConfigObject = {
   717→    devtool?: string | boolean;
   718→    plugins?: Array<WebpackPluginInstance>;
   719→    entry: WebpackEntryProperty;
   720→    output: {
   721→        filename: string;
   722→        path: string;
   723→    };
   724→    target: string;
   725→    context: string;
   726→    ignoreWarnings?: IgnoreWarningsOption;
   727→    resolve?: {
   728→        modules?: string[];
   729→        alias?: {
   730→            [key: string]: string | boolean;
   731→        };
   732→    };
   733→    module?: {
   734→        rules: Array<WebpackModuleRule>;
   735→    };
   736→} & {
   737→    [key: string]: unknown;
   738→};
   739→export type WebpackConfigObjectWithModuleRules = WebpackConfigObject & Required<Pick<WebpackConfigObject, 'module'>>;
   740→export type BuildContext = {
   741→    dev: boolean;
   742→    isServer: boolean;
   743→    buildId: string;
   744→    dir: string;
   745→    config: any;
   746→    webpack: {
   747→        version: string;
   748→        DefinePlugin: new (values: Record<string, string | boolean>) => WebpackPluginInstance;
   749→        ProvidePlugin: new (values: Record<string, string | string[]>) => WebpackPluginInstance;
   750→    };
   751→    defaultLoaders: any;
   752→    totalPages: number;
   753→    nextRuntime?: 'nodejs' | 'edge';
   754→};
   755→/**
   756→ * Webpack `entry` config
   757→ */
   758→export type WebpackEntryProperty = EntryPropertyObject | EntryPropertyFunction;
   759→export type EntryPropertyObject = {
   760→    [key: string]: EntryPointValue;
   761→};
   762→export type EntryPropertyFunction = () => Promise<EntryPropertyObject>;
   763→export type EntryPointValue = string | Array<string> | EntryPointObject;
   764→export type EntryPointObject = {
   765→    import: string | Array<string>;
   766→};
   767→/**
   768→ * Webpack `module.rules` entry
   769→ */
   770→export type WebpackModuleRule = {
   771→    test?: string | RegExp | ((resourcePath: string) => boolean);
   772→    include?: Array<string | RegExp> | RegExp;
   773→    exclude?: (filepath: string) => boolean;
   774→    use?: ModuleRuleUseProperty | Array<ModuleRuleUseProperty>;
   775→    oneOf?: Array<WebpackModuleRule>;
   776→};
   777→export type ModuleRuleUseProperty = {
   778→    loader?: string;
   779→    options?: Record<string, unknown>;
   780→};
   781→/**
   782→ * Global with values we add when we inject code into people's pages, for use at runtime.
   783→ */
   784→export type EnhancedGlobal = typeof GLOBAL_OBJ & {
   785→    _sentryRewriteFramesDistDir?: string;
   786→    SENTRY_RELEASE?: {
   787→        id: string;
   788→    };
   789→    SENTRY_RELEASES?: {
   790→        [key: string]: {
   791→            id: string;
   792→        };
   793→    };
   794→};
   795→export type JSONValue = string | number | boolean | JSONValue[] | {
   796→    [k: string]: JSONValue;
   797→};
   798→type TurbopackLoaderItem = string | {
   799→    loader: string;
   800→    options: Record<string, JSONValue>;
   801→};
   802→type TurbopackRuleCondition = {
   803→    path: string | RegExp;
   804→};
   805→type TurbopackRuleConditionFilter = string | {
   806→    not: TurbopackRuleConditionFilter;
   807→} | {
   808→    all: TurbopackRuleConditionFilter[];
   809→} | {
   810→    any: TurbopackRuleConditionFilter[];
   811→} | {
   812→    path: string | RegExp;
   813→} | {
   814→    content: RegExp;
   815→};
   816→export type TurbopackRuleConfigItemOrShortcut = TurbopackLoaderItem[] | TurbopackRuleConfigItem;
   817→export type TurbopackMatcherWithRule = {
   818→    matcher: string;
   819→    rule: TurbopackRuleConfigItemOrShortcut;
   820→};
   821→type TurbopackRuleConfigItemOptions = {
   822→    loaders: TurbopackLoaderItem[];
   823→    as?: string;
   824→    condition?: TurbopackRuleConditionFilter;
   825→};
   826→type TurbopackRuleConfigItem = TurbopackRuleConfigItemOptions | {
   827→    [condition: string]: TurbopackRuleConfigItem;
   828→} | false;
   829→export interface TurbopackOptions {
   830→    resolveAlias?: Record<string, string | string[] | Record<string, string | string[]>>;
   831→    resolveExtensions?: string[];
   832→    rules?: Record<string, TurbopackRuleConfigItemOrShortcut>;
   833→    conditions?: Record<string, TurbopackRuleCondition>;
   834→    moduleIds?: 'named' | 'deterministic';
   835→    root?: string;
   836→    debugIds?: boolean;
   837→}
   838→export {};
